content:
I usually don't upgrade right away when a new Apple Watch comes out. I was using the Apple Watch Series 10, which launched in September 2024, but I only bought it this January. However, even though the Apple Watch Series 12 looks almost identical to the Series 10, it's still incredibly tempting to pick one up, and here's why.

That's right, the Series 10 and Series 12 are essentially the same design. In fact, the Series 12's bezels are ever so slightly thicker, which is technically a downgrade. But that doesn't bother me at all, since I use a black watch face anyway.

That said, the new features on the Apple Watch Series 12 are genuinely exciting to me. In particular, the massively improved heart rate monitoring and the brand new Readiness app are hugely appealing. Overall performance on the Series 12 is noticeably snappier too, especially with Siri.

Previous Apple Watches never quite delivered what I wanted in terms of health tracking. The Series 12 gives you so much more useful information. Before, it was basically just the activity rings and a bunch of scattered data in the Health app. Now, the new Health app lays out everything you need to know in a remarkably useful way.

I'm still wearing my WHOOP for now, mainly because I want to compare them over a longer period before deciding to drop it entirely, but so far Apple's Health app holds up impressively well, and I'm genuinely pleased with the Series 12's health tracking capabilities.

Top comment: Nutmac

Michael didn't mention the battery life improvement, but it's actually quite significant. With my typical usage, I can easily get well over 24 hours on a single charge.

It's also worth noting that WHOOP costs $239 per year for its subscription, and it no longer offers much of a clear advantage over Apple's Health app.

All in all, the reason I bought the Apple Watch Series 12 can be summed up in one sentence: Apple is making a serious push into the health wearables space, and the Apple Watch no longer feels like an optional extra.
